hook: How a compost tumbler really works

slides.t: A closed drum on a stand. You turn it by hand to mix and air the pile, so there is no forking or digging.
Fill one side while the other side finishes. When the first is done, empty it and start again.
Mix kitchen scraps with dry leaves, straw or torn cardboard. Roughly two or three parts brown to one part green.
It should feel like a wrung-out sponge. Too wet and it smells sour, so add browns. Too dry, add a little water.
Leave out meat, dairy and oily food. Turn it a few times a week. In cold weather it slows down, and that is normal.

hook: A gift for the gardener who has everything
hook_sub: Fresh herbs on the counter all winter

slides.t: A small countertop garden. Plants grow in water with nutrients instead of soil, under a built-in grow light.
Drop seed pods in, fill the tank, add plant food as the directions say and set the light timer. That is it.
Leafy herbs like basil, parsley and mint, plus lettuce and other greens. Big crops need a much bigger setup.
Enough pods for what they cook, a light that can rise as plants grow, and a tank that is easy to top up.
Keep the water filled and trim herbs often so they bush out. Clean the tank between plantings.
